findings.evidence: i5695 p. 3, Joint occupancy: within every aggregate limit no allocation is needed, but sharing draws Yes. Safe; as group 4 finding 1.

i5695 p. 3: the question's parenthetical '(whether or not the other occupant files Form 5695, and whether you paid for the same items or for different ones)' and 'answer Yes if you shared any one of them' fix the occupancy reading; a No by a filer whose co-occupant bought separate items needs a reading the question rules out. Low.

unruled:f8960.unsupported.reason: No defect; as group 9. Findings 0 to 3 are covered by sibling screens, 4 and 5 are the accepted WIDE findings, 6 and 7 are covered. The restructuring drew no finding of a narrowed item.

findings.evidence: i8960 pp. 13-14. f8960.refund asks about any recovery or refund of an amount deducted on an earlier Form 8960 (naming a state income tax refund) and gates the same lines. As group 9 finding 0.
i8960 p. 13. Form 8814: scope.other_line16 ("filing Form 8814 (even with no tax)") refuses the return. As group 9 finding 1.
i8960 p. 13. Substitute interest and dividend payments and notional principal contract payments are Schedule 1 line 8z kinds refused by oi8z and s1.line8_other. As group 9 finding 2.
i8960 p. 13. A casualty or theft loss is refused by sa.unsupported. As group 9 finding 3.
i8960 p. 7: qualified-plan annuities draw Yes though line 3 is zero. Safe; as group 9 finding 5.
i8960 pp. 7, 22: Form 8815 draws Yes though line 1 and MAGI are right. Safe; as group 9 finding 6.

i8960 p. 13. A Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) is refused by scope.schedule1 ("estates or trusts ... Schedule K-1"); reading RIC or REIT dividends as pass-through income draws only a safe Yes. As group 9 finding 7.

i8960 p. 18, Line 9b. A deduction of foreign income tax on Schedule A is refused by sa.unsupported ("a foreign tax or generation-skipping tax deduction"), whichever way the filer reads the investment-expense item.

unruled:gift.special.reason: No defect. Findings 0 and 2 accepted WIDE; finding 1 accepted (minor UNCLEAR, leans WIDE), as group 7 finding 0.

findings.evidence: i8283 p. 3, item 2.d: securities that qualify under Regulations section 1.170A-13(c)(7)(xi)(B) but are not publicly traded as the question defines it draw Yes and are refused though Section A would do. Safe.

i8283 pp. 1, 3. The question asks about "a deduction over $5,000 (before any income limit), or property worth more than $5,000", so property worth over $5,000 with a reduced deduction of $5,000 or less draws Yes and is refused though the helper computes it. Safe (as group 7 finding 0).
i8283 p. 3: partial interests and property with use restrictions need Section B only above $5,000; the question's item has no threshold, so smaller gifts are refused. Safe.

unruled:person.x_other.reason: No defect. Findings 0 and 1 accepted WIDE, as the prior review's 0 and 2; finding 2 accepted (minor UNCLEAR, leans WIDE), the prior finding 3 read as unclear. The restructuring drew no finding of a narrowed item.

findings.evidence: i5329 p. 9. An ABLE (or Coverdell) excess returned in time answers Yes: a harmless over-refusal, as the prior finding 0.
i5329 p. 9. An RMD shortfall whose deadline fell outside 2025 answers Yes: a harmless over-refusal, as the prior finding 2.

f5329 p. 2, Part VII. An earlier-year HSA excess absorbed during 2025: a filer who answers Yes is refused (safe); one who answers No has no prior-year excess left for line 46, and the 2025 excess is figured by f8889 (as the prior finding 3, accepted). The item's words are unchanged by R4.

unruled:refund.not_2024.reason: No defect. One WIDE (non-itemizer refused though line 1 is zero), as group 4 finding 2. PENDING-4-7 (2024 tax paid before 2024) closed by credits-misc PENDING-5; the screen widened only.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 88; p525 p. 24: a 2024 non-itemizer or sales-tax elector who paid part of 2024 tax in 2025 answers Yes and is refused though the taxable refund is zero. Safe; as group 4 finding 2.

unruled:retirement.special.reason: No defect. Findings 0, 2 and 3 repeat the prior findings 0, 1 and 4; finding 1 (a conversion of another IRA) is covered because the conversion is itself a Form 1099-R entry on which the filer answers Yes (screen groups 2 and 4). The R2 restructure (one bullet per item, items in their original order and each multi-part item kept whole) drew no finding on its own wording.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 27, Exception 2, 'Distribution code T is shown in box 7'. retirement.bad_code refuses a roth_ira account with any code other than qualified_roth_Q (and Q from any other account) and gates the same lines, so a nonqualified or code T Roth IRA distribution is refused whatever this answer. As the prior finding 0.

i1040gi p. 27, Exception 2, 'You converted part or all of a traditional IRA or traditional SIMPLE IRA to a Roth IRA in 2025.' A 2025 conversion is reported on its own Form 1099-R, which the filer enters; on that entry 'a conversion or recharacterization (Form 8606)' is Yes and the return is refused, so the separate distribution is never computed alone (as screen group 2 finding 5 and group 4 finding 1). The item's words are unchanged by R2.

p575 p. 17, 'Cost of contract x Amount received / Account balance = Tax-free amount'. The payer reports that tax-free part in box 5, which retirement.plan_simple subtracts (retirement.plan_excluded) for any plan distribution, periodic or not, with the rolled-over amount; the reviewer's premise that only the Simplified Method recovers cost is wrong. As the prior finding 1.
i1040gi p. 27, Exception 2, item 1. A pension or qualified Roth filer with nondeductible traditional IRA basis may answer Yes and be refused; refusal only. As the prior finding 4.

unruled:s1.alimony_unsupported.reason: No defect. Findings 0 and 1 covered by s1.alimony and the amount questions s1.alimony_received and s1.alimony_paid (as the prior findings 0, 1 and 5); 2 and 3 accepted WIDE (prior 3 and 4); 4 accepted (minor UNCLEAR, leans WIDE). The prior defect (payments within one household, PENDING-7-3) did not recur: the amount questions now exclude those payments. The nested list keeps the original order and grammar ("payments of which part is not alimony: child support ..., payments for a home ..., or payments of which any part must continue ...").

findings.evidence: p504 p. 16, Example 2; i1040gi p. 89. s1.alimony counts "only payments made before any change after 2018 that expressly applies the post-2018 rules", and s1.alimony_received and s1.alimony_paid exclude "payments made after the agreement was changed after 2018 in a way that expressly applies the post-2018 rules", so only the payments before the change are entered (as the prior finding 5).

p504 p. 13, Payments not alimony. s1.alimony_received and s1.alimony_paid list under "Do not include" child support, noncash property settlements, the spouse's part of community income and payments to keep up or the use of the payer's property, so those parts are never entered as alimony (as the prior findings 0 and 1).
p504 p. 13, Payments to a third party, Example 2: a home owned only by the recipient is fully alimony but answers Yes. Safe; as the prior finding 3.
p504 p. 16: a decrease with no recapture is refused. Safe; as the prior finding 4.
p504 p. 16. A filer whose first 3 calendar years ended before 2025 answers Yes (refused, safe) or No (correct: no recapture is reportable in 2025).

unruled:s1.cod_unsupported.reason: No defect. Finding 0 accepted WIDE (the prior finding 1); finding 1 covered by the help; finding 2 accepted (minor UNCLEAR, leans WIDE). The prior NARROW (short sale) did not recur.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 20. Nondeductible personal interest in Form 1099-C box 3 draws Yes and is refused though box 2 is fully taxable. Safe; as the prior finding 1.

p4681 p. 6. The question's help gives the insolvency test and its timing: "for example insolvency, when your debts were more than the value of everything you owned just before the cancellation"; everything owned includes retirement accounts, so a filer following the help reads insolvency as Pub. 4681 defines it.

f1099c p. 4, Box 5: "Shows whether you were personally liable for repayment of the debt". The item asks whether you were not personally liable and points to the box that shows it; Form 1099-C's box 5 caption (p. 2) asks to check it if the debtor was personally liable. The item's words are unchanged by R4.

unruled:s1.uc_unsupported.reason: No defect. Three WIDE (accepted, as group 4); PENDING-4-9 closed by income PENDING-2, a widening. The paystub-label UNCLEAR is presentation: the question follows the i1040gi wording and the ambiguity is in the filer's records (low).

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 89: a repayment of $3,000 or less of earlier-year compensation is refused though line 7 is unaffected. Safe; as group 4 finding 1.
i1040gi p. 89: contributions with no 2025 compensation. The screen is asked under s1.has_uc, and line 7 is zero either way. Safe; as group 4 finding 0.
i1040gi p. 89: earlier-year contributions already recovered draw Yes; refused though computable. Safe.

i1040gi p. 89 Caution and TIP: the question names unemployment contributions and excludes paid family leave and disability contributions, as the source does. A combined paystub label is a records question no rewording resolves; the cost of a wrong No is line 7 not reduced by the contribution. Low.

unruled:sales.special.reason: No defect. Findings 0 and 1 accepted WIDE (as group 12); finding 2 accepted (minor UNCLEAR, leans WIDE).

findings.evidence: i1040sd p. 12, Line 19. An S corporation or trust interest whose entity holds only section 1250 property is refused though no line 19 look-through entry results. Safe; as group 12 finding 0.
i1040sd pp. 11-12, Lines 18 and 19: a loss sale, or a sale of an interest held 1 year or less, needs no worksheet entry, but the item draws Yes. Safe.

i1040sd p. 11, Line 19. A filer who reads REIT or C corporation stock as involving depreciable real property answers Yes and is refused; the item's own words ("depreciable real property (section 1250 property: generally, real property for which depreciation was allowed or allowable ...)") are the filer's property. Safe.

unruled:sb.line8.reason: As the earlier ruling: the adjustments are screened by sb.unsupported; WIDE accepted.

findings.evidence: sb.unsupported ('Any nominee income, original issue discount reported in an amount other than on Form 1099-OID, accrued interest paid on a bond purchase, bond premium adjustment, ... a savings bond interest exclusion, or other special treatment?') refuses lines 2, 3 and 6 through its gate line sb.unsupported_if_income, and is asked whenever taxable interest, ordinary dividends or capital gain distributions are above zero, which every situation in this finding has (the interest roster's help names savings bonds, OID, accrued and seller-financed interest and nominee interest).

sb.unsupported ('Any nominee income, original issue discount reported in an amount other than on Form 1099-OID, accrued interest paid on a bond purchase, bond premium adjustment, ... a savings bond interest exclusion, or other special treatment?') refuses lines 2, 3 and 6 through its gate line sb.unsupported_if_income, and is asked whenever taxable interest, ordinary dividends or capital gain distributions are above zero, which every situation in this finding has (the interest roster's help names savings bonds, OID, accrued and seller-financed interest and nominee interest).

sb.unsupported ('Any nominee income, original issue discount reported in an amount other than on Form 1099-OID, accrued interest paid on a bond purchase, bond premium adjustment, ... a savings bond interest exclusion, or other special treatment?') refuses lines 2, 3 and 6 through its gate line sb.unsupported_if_income, and is asked whenever taxable interest, ordinary dividends or capital gain distributions are above zero, which every situation in this finding has (the interest roster's help names savings bonds, OID, accrued and seller-financed interest and nominee interest).
Refuses lines the tool would compute; safe.

i1040sb p. 3: 'a loan of cash or marketable securities is generally considered to be a distribution'; the question counts every loan, so the residual reading errs toward yes (BUG-0246 widening, as the earlier ruling).

unruled:scope.other_line16.reason: One low defect in wording R0 kept unchanged (BUG-0433, the Form 8615 condition omits the IRS examples of unearned income); the CFC/PFIC findings are the accepted over-refusal; 965(i) falls under the opening clause.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 36. As the prior ruling (finding 3): a triggered section 965(i) liability is an 'additional Form 1040 line 16 tax' under the question's opening clause, which the list only illustrates. Rare.
i8960 p. 22; i1040gi p. 34. Any CFC or PFIC stock, and Form 8621, is refused even with no line 16 tax (BUG-0409, accepted over-refusal). Safe.

i1040gi p. 36: 'more than $2,700 of unearned income (such as taxable interest, ordinary dividends, or capital gains (including capital gain distributions))'. The question gives the threshold without the examples, so a child with mostly capital gains may answer No and Form 8615 tax is missed. The words are the prior wording's (R0 changed none); BUG-0433, low.

unruled:scope.schedule1.reason: No defect, after the second round: the first round's UNCLEAR on alimony paid came from R0 sorting 'alimony under an agreement made before 2019' under income, which narrowed it to alimony received (s1.alimony asks received or paid); the list was restored to the original order and the review rerun, which raised no such finding. The NARROW findings are covered by other gates; the WIDE and UNCLEAR ones can only refuse.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 40: a passive Schedule C answers sc.passive No and is refused (sc.screened refuses sc.line1), and scope.other_income asks 'income or loss from a passive activity'. As the prior ruling (finding 0).
i1040gi p. 104: s1.sc_1a (from sc.tips_ot) refuses s1a.line5_calc for qualified tips received in a trade or business. As the prior ruling (finding 1).
i1040gi p. 108: s1.sc_1a (from sc.tips_ot) refuses s1a.line14b_calc for overtime on Form 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC. As the prior ruling (finding 2).
i1040sc p. 5, Line 1, Statutory employees: a statutory employee's Schedule C answers sc.statutory Yes and is refused (sc.screened); either reading of this question refuses.
i1040gi p. 42; i1040sse p. 1: church wages under $108.28 are refused though line 1z is right. Safe; as the prior ruling (finding 3).

i1040gi p. 40, Step 2 question 4. A Yes refuses; a No leaves a business rental of personal property on Schedule C, where a rental activity answers sc.passive No and sc.screened refuses it. Either answer refuses or computes correctly.

unruled:ssb.terror_disability.reason: Round-1 PENDING-3-4 closed ('eligible for coverage ... whether or not you made a claim'); the full-retirement-age finding remains WIDE (T-008).

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 31: Benefits after full retirement age read as disability payments: yes refuses what the tool computes. Safe (T-008, round 1).

unruled:refund.box8.reason: No defect: the UNCLEAR reading errs only toward YES (refusal of a refund the tool computes), and the nontaxable business-tax refund is refused; both accepted WIDE.

findings.evidence: f1099g p. 5 Box 8: 'an income tax that applies exclusively to income from a trade or business and is not a tax of general application'. The misreading the model describes (a general income tax that in the filer's case reached only business income) yields YES and a refusal (eval: stage16.mut.refund_single_unasked with refund.box8 yes -> refund.taxable, s1.line1, f1040.line11a, f1040.line24 refuse on gate refund.box8; with no, s1.line1 $1,400.00). The opposite error, a business-only tax answered NO, is not invited: the question names the kind of tax and gives box 8 as the example. Safe; adding 'not a tax of general application' would sharpen it (optional).

A business-only income tax refund never deducted is refused although the tool's zero would be right (f1099g p. 5: 'If taxable, report the amount in box 2 on Schedule C or F'). Refusal is safe; same disposition as group 3 finding 1.

unruled:f8962.alloc.reason: No defect. One WIDE: a policy member in no tax family is 'not in' the filer's tax family and draws Yes though no Part IV allocation applies; f8962.other also refuses APTC for someone in no one's tax family. Safe.

findings.evidence: i8962 pp. 12, 17: allocation is for 'at least one individual in another tax family'; a member in no tax family draws Yes here, and f8962.other ('advance payments were made for someone who is in no one's tax family') refuses the same lines anyway. Safe.

unruled:f8962.other.reason: No defect. Four WIDE and one UNCLEAR that leans WIDE: each reading that matters gives Yes and refuses f8962.line24 and line25; no reading lets an unsupported case compute. Findings 0, 1, 2 and 4 repeat the prior findings 0, 2, 1 and 4; finding 3 (post-employment coverage offered and not enrolled in) is new and WIDE. The R2 restructure (the coverage kinds as a nested list under the eligibility item) drew no finding on its own wording.

findings.evidence: i8962 p. 4: MEC eligibility of a tax family member not enrolled in a qualified health plan does not change the coverage family; 'anyone in your tax family' refuses. Safe; as the prior finding 0.

i8962 p. 5, 'you gave accurate information about the availability of employer coverage to the Marketplace, and the Marketplace determined that you were eligible for APTC': such an offer is not affordable, but the 9.02% item draws Yes and refuses. Safe; as the prior finding 2.

i8962 p. 6, a Medicaid or CHIP ineligibility determination on accurate information holds 'even if your actual 2025 income suggests that the individual may have been eligible'; the Medicaid item draws Yes and refuses. Safe; as the prior finding 1.

i8962 p. 6, 'you are not considered eligible for that post-employment coverage unless you actually enroll in the coverage'. A former employee offered affordable COBRA or retiree coverage and not enrolled may answer Yes on the offered-coverage item and is refused; refusal only. The words are unchanged by R2.

i8962 p. 3, 'An individual is generally considered eligible for MEC for the month only if they were eligible for every day of the month'. Partial-month eligibility read as 'for any month' gives Yes and refuses; under the every-day rule No is also right. Safe; as the prior finding 4.

unruled:f8962.premium_adjust.reason: No defect. Two WIDE and one UNCLEAR that leans WIDE: every Yes refuses f8962.line24 and line25, and the No reading of the UNCLEAR case computes from column A as reported, which the reviewer itself calls correct. The prior unpaid-premium NARROW did not recur; the refund finding repeats the prior finding 1.

findings.evidence: i8962 p. 18, Line 25, 'Enter the amount from line 11(f) or add lines 12(f) through 23(f)'. Line 25 is the APTC from Form 1095-A column C, which neither adjustment changes; refusing line 25 with line 24 on a Yes refuses a value the tool could compute. Refusal only.

i8962 p. 4, 'The enrollment premiums are the total amount of the premiums for the month, reduced by any premium amounts for that month that were refunded in 2025'. A refund already netted in column A draws Yes and is refused though column A as reported is right; any refund draws Yes, so no reading lets an unreflected refund compute. Safe; as the prior finding 1.

i8962 p. 4, 'Generally, if coverage in a qualified health plan began after the first day of the month, you are not allowed a monthly credit amount for the coverage for that month.' Mid-month coverage asked by its start date gives Yes and refuses; a filer answering No because column A already shows nothing for the partial month computes that month from column A as reported, which the finding itself says the tool treats correctly. Safe.

unruled:sa.dependent.reason: No defect: the parenthetical is the Form 1040 dependent-question carve-out, not an EIC import. i1040gi pp. 18–19, Step 4/5: "If the person who could claim you on their 2025 tax return is not required to file, and isn’t filing a 2025 tax return or is filing a 2025 return only to claim a refund of withheld income tax or estimated tax paid, check ‘No.’" The reviewer's pages (34–35, 41–42) do not include pp. 18–19. The line 12a checkbox and the Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents use that answer, so a filer in the carve-out is not claimable for this purpose and the full standard deduction is right.

unruled:s8812.puerto_rico.reason: WIDE only; each finding refuses a Puerto Rico resident whose line 27 or line 11 the non-Puerto Rico computation already gets right.

findings.evidence: f1040s8812 p. 2, line 16b Yes branch: with line 20 at least line 17, line 27 is line 17 on either branch; the resident is refused though the tool's value is right. The help says "If you are not sure, answer Yes". Safe.
i1040s8812 p. 5, CLW B line 6: with line 5 not less than line 1, lines 7 to 10 are blank and line 11 is 0 for a resident too; refused though the tool computes 0. Safe.
f1040s8812 p. 2, line 16a ("If zero, stop here") and line 16b: Part II-B is never reached, line 27 is 0; refused for nothing. Safe.

unruled:sb.form5471.reason: No defect: WIDE by design (the tool refuses a return that may need Form 5471, which it does not prepare); the question names you or your spouse.

findings.evidence: A spouse's role refuses a head-of-household return; Form 5471 is outside the tool either way. Safe.

unruled:gate:div.has_ordinary.reason: No defect: dividends without a form are part of box 1a as the tool asks it; Form 8814 is refused before these lines.

findings.evidence: Form 8814 is refused by scope.other_line16 ('filing Form 8814 (even with no tax)'), asked of every filer.

i1040gi p. 25: 'Qualified dividends are also included in the ordinary dividend total required to be shown on line 3b'; the box 1a question's help asks for 'any ordinary dividends received without a form', and div.any names dividends received without any form.
Refuses lines the tool would compute; safe.

unruled:gate:sb.has_income.reason: No defect: the interest roster's help names each case; the WIDE item is the nominee capital gain distribution limb (i1040gi p. 33).

findings.evidence: the interest payer roster's help names original issue discount, accrued market discount (taxable even on a tax-exempt bond), contingent payment debt instrument gain, U.S. savings bonds even when the interest may be excluded, a buyer paying interest on seller financing, and nominee interest, so each is entered as interest and makes sb.has_income true.

the interest payer roster's help names original issue discount, accrued market discount (taxable even on a tax-exempt bond), contingent payment debt instrument gain, U.S. savings bonds even when the interest may be excluded, a buyer paying interest on seller financing, and nominee interest, so each is entered as interest and makes sb.has_income true.
i1040gi p. 33, line 7a: nominee capital gain distributions; the special-treatment question names nominee income. One extra question; safe.

unruled:f8889.unsupported.reason: No defect in the screen: the NARROW finding is a fiscal-year filer, outside the whole tool (calendar-year 2025 returns; the fiscal-year refusing row of the gate grids), not a gap of this screen. Rerun after the refusal text of f8889.unsupported named the person who died in 2025 (owner decision 2026-11-07); the WIDE finding of the earlier review did not recur.

findings.evidence: i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, 'the 1st day of the last month of the tax year (December 1, for most individuals)'. A fiscal-year filer's last month is not December, but the tool prepares calendar-year returns throughout (every form's dates assume it); the gate grids carry a fiscal-year refusing row. The decedent clause added here is the owner's decision for a person who died in 2025 (BUG-0452).
